title: POSIX SSH execution providers
summary: Remote execution uses an OpenSSH alias to reach a POSIX helper installed on the remote host; the filesystem, subprocess and sandbox providers share that helper, with separate SSH channels for administration and for each program stream.
firstReason: SSH as the remote execution world is kept; a Go helper binary is easy to cross-compile and install, and the provider structure stays the same.

title: Session writable-directory effects
summary: A plugin can grant one live session write access to an extra directory. The grant is an effect that ends when the plugin unloads and is not restored from history on resume or fork. An invalid extra path stops execution with a named error.
firstReason: Deployment-wide roots cannot express a grant for one session, or one that ends with its plugin. Effect-scoped grants map directly onto the Go cordis lifecycle. Disposal affects later operations only; processes already running keep their launch grants, which is a stated limit.

title: Windows additional directory grants stay in file tools
summary: On Windows, extra writable directories granted to a session are enforced only by the harness file tools (`write`, `edit`); sandboxed processes keep workspace and private-temp access only. The model is told the difference.
firstReason: This is a recorded limitation: extending the ACL-based process sandbox per directory was judged too fragile. The first verdict keeps it; the sandbox area decides whether a Go Windows backend can enforce extra roots and so remove the limit.

title: Windows sandbox rung: raw ACL restricted tokens over mxc and AppContainer
summary: The Windows sandbox confines writes with a `WRITE_RESTRICTED` token whose restricting SIDs carry workspace and private-temp capabilities, lowered to Low integrity, with matching access-control entries and Low labels on the granted directories. It is built directly on raw Win32 ACL calls, not on mxc or AppContainer.
firstReason: Windows needs a real confining executor, or shipped profiles fall back to full access. The mechanism is operating-system API calls that Go can make through its Windows system-call packages, and the reasoning about delete rights carries over unchanged.

title: Windows sandbox delete confinement: mandatory integrity plus an ambient-delete deny
summary: Each Windows sandbox grant applies three edits in one call: the capability allow entry, a deny of `FILE_DELETE_CHILD` for everyone on containers, and a Low integrity label, with the token lowered to Low. Together they stop a confined process deleting files outside its granted roots through the parent directory's delete right.
firstReason: It closes a real escape (deleting files outside the workspace) in the restricted-token sandbox. The fix is Windows security semantics and must be carried over exactly, with tests that try the escape.

title: Parse SSH policies once at request admission
summary: Proposal: the SSH helper validates a sandbox policy once, when the request arrives, and passes the typed result on; the inner resolver no longer validates it a second time.
firstReason: Adopt: decoding once at the wire boundary into a typed value is the ordinary Go shape, and the typed parameter states the precondition.

title: Canonicalize each sandbox workspace once
summary: Proposal: resolve the real path of a sandbox workspace once per confinement, in the code that derives the roots, instead of once in common preprocessing and again in each backend.
firstReason: Adopt: one canonical workspace path per call avoids repeated filesystem work and, more importantly, avoids two resolutions that could disagree if the path changes between them.
